Not the masculine participle (טוען…). Use the Hebrew ellipsis character … as in English.
Straight double quotes around inserted names; no gershayim abbreviations (write words in full).

Start every text with a Hebrew word where natural: Slint takes a paragraph's direction from its first strong letter, so a text that starts with eov, a Latin term or a placeholder is laid out left to right. Where a text must start that way, it starts with U+200F (RIGHT-TO-LEFT MARK); `import` adds it and `check` requires it (docs/translating.md, "Right-to-left languages").

Wrap a left-to-right fragment that contains punctuation (an extension such as .eop, an option such as --language, a path such as ~/.cargo, a number with its unit, a range, w × h, a config example) in U+2068 (FIRST STRONG ISOLATE) … U+2069 (POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE), or it is drawn as eop. or language--. Not U+200E: a mark stops protecting the fragment once eov isolates the value inside it.

Units, ×, keys and Latin-script names as written; eov isolates inserted values in right-to-left text. Percent sign directly after the number (50%), as in Hebrew typesetting; a space before it would put it on the wrong side.
